tools.name: keyframe_open
tools.description: Open or resume a saved editor session in a dedicated Chrome profile. Call first; waits for project restoration.

tools.name: keyframe_methods
tools.description: List scripting methods; read recipes through keyframe_call for rigging workflows.

tools.name: keyframe_call
tools.description: Call a scripting method using positional arguments. Read keyframe_methods first. Mutations are saved; image results appear inline.

tools.name: keyframe_screenshot
tools.description: Show the editor UI. Prefer contact sheets to assess animation.

tools.name: keyframe_session
tools.description: Read active project, readiness and revision. Supply expected to edit tools to reject stale edits.

tools.name: keyframe_list_projects
tools.description: List projects saved in this connector profile.

tools.name: keyframe_open_project
tools.description: Save the active project and open a saved project by ID.

tools.name: keyframe_save
tools.description: Wait for the active project to commit to browser storage.

tools.name: keyframe_build_animation
tools.description: Build a complete clip atomically. Partial transforms carry forward from setup. loop:true copies the first pose to the end. replace:true replaces a clip and all its tracks. FPS is project-wide.

tools.name: keyframe_configure_animation
tools.description: Set clip duration and project FPS. Rejects shortening past keys/events.

tools.name: keyframe_apply_pose
tools.description: Apply bone transforms at a time in the active clip. Validates all names and values before editing. Use build_animation for a whole clip.

tools.name: keyframe_contact_sheet
tools.description: Show sampled frames with timestamps, empty frames and edge-touch warnings. Uses a fixed camera fitted to the clip; warnings indicate possible clipping.

tools.name: keyframe_check_animation
tools.description: Check endpoint discontinuities, sampled invisible parts and rig problems. Warnings can be intentional; also review rendered frames.

tools.name: keyframe_export
tools.description: Write an editable project JSON, animated GIF or Spine ZIP to disk. Returns an MCP resource and local path. Spine ZIP includes atlas, textures and a preview.

tools.name: keyframe_image_layers
tools.description: List editable image layers and stable IDs in bottom-to-top order.

tools.name: keyframe_image_layer_png
tools.description: Show one image layer as a PNG.

tools.name: keyframe_edit_image_layers
tools.description: Atomically add text or embedded image layers, edit properties/text, reorder or delete layers. Updates composite and editable layers. Close the human image editor first.

tools.name: keyframe_open_result
tools.description: Save the project and show it in visible Chrome with the connector profile. Export project JSON to transfer to your usual browser.

tools.name: puppeteer_open
tools.description: Open Sprite Puppeteer (pixel-art sprite rigging, animation and play-testing) in the connector profile; optionally load a sample: "orc" or "knight" (sprite sheets: side, isometric, top-down) or "golem" (rigged). Returns the character state. Call first.

tools.name: puppeteer_methods
tools.description: List every Sprite Puppeteer scripting method with arguments, plus recipes. Reach methods without a named tool through puppeteer_call.

tools.name: puppeteer_call
tools.description: Call any window.spritePuppeteer method with positional arguments. Read puppeteer_methods first. Image results appear inline; exports become files.

tools.name: puppeteer_state
tools.description: Current character: kind (rigged or sprite-sheet), moves, camera set and direction or views, settings, project.

tools.name: puppeteer_play_move
tools.description: Show a move on the stage, optionally from a time or paused.

tools.name: puppeteer_set_view
tools.description: Sprite sheets: camera set (side, iso8, topdown8, topdown4…) and direction (S = facing down). Rigged: drawn view (side, front, back, fq, bq). Both: facing 1 (right) or -1 (left).

tools.name: puppeteer_settings
tools.description: Change settings through the panel: background (checker is transparent in exports), fps, pixel scale, speed, exaggeration, effects, export format, one/all moves, 4/8 directions.

tools.name: puppeteer_move_guide
tools.description: Rigged characters: pose channels with units, ranges and rest values, animation conventions, eases, events and the JSON shape for puppeteer_create_move. Read before creating a move.

tools.name: puppeteer_create_move
tools.description: Rigged characters: add a keyframed move. keys list only channels that differ from rest; a loop flows back to its first key. replace: an existing custom move id to overwrite (keeps its id and hotkey).

tools.name: puppeteer_contact_sheet
tools.description: A labelled grid of a move's frames (cells about 220 px): the way to judge a move. Defaults to the current move.

tools.name: puppeteer_render_frame
tools.description: One frame of a move as a PNG, transparent unless background:true.

tools.name: puppeteer_load_image
tools.description: Load a sprite from the local disk as a new rigged character (PNG, GIF, WebP, JPEG, .aseprite/.ase or .psd; layers keep their names). The skeleton auto-fits; check with puppeteer_contact_sheet.

tools.name: puppeteer_export
tools.description: Write an export to disk: sheet (PNG + Aseprite-style JSON), godot, unity, gm (GameMaker), frames (PNG zip), spine (rigged only), gif (one move) or project (.puppet.json). moves: current or all; dirs: view, 4 or 8.

tools.name: puppeteer_list_projects
tools.description: List Sprite Puppeteer projects saved in this connector profile.

tools.name: puppeteer_open_project
tools.description: Open a saved Sprite Puppeteer project by ID.

tools.name: puppeteer_save
tools.description: Save the current character as a project, optionally naming it.

tools.name: puppeteer_screenshot
tools.description: Show the Sprite Puppeteer page. Prefer puppeteer_contact_sheet to judge motion.

tools.name: puppeteer_open_result
tools.description: Save and show Sprite Puppeteer in visible Chrome with the connector profile, so the user can keep working.

tools.name: meshforge_open
tools.description: Open MeshForge (3D models: rig in the browser, animate from keyframe specs, prop bones, sprite sheets) in the connector profile, optionally opening a library model by id or name. A new profile starts with the example orc (rigged, 18 clips). Call first.

tools.name: meshforge_methods
tools.description: List every MeshForge scripting method (window.meshforge) with arguments, plus recipes. Reach methods without a named tool through meshforge_call.

tools.name: meshforge_call
tools.description: Call any window.meshforge method with positional arguments. Read meshforge_methods first. Images appear inline; exports become files.

tools.name: meshforge_state
tools.description: The open model (rigged? bone count, height), its animations, what is playing, any rig draft, unsaved changes.

tools.name: meshforge_models
tools.description: The MeshForge library in this connector profile: id, name, label (how it was made), status.

tools.name: meshforge_open_model
tools.description: Open a library model in the viewer by id or name.

tools.name: meshforge_import_model
tools.description: Add a .glb from the local disk to the library and open it.

tools.name: meshforge_generate
tools.description: Image → textured 3D model on the user's own fal.ai key (PAID unless MeshForge is in demo mode: ask the user first and pass confirmCost:true). image: a local PNG/JPEG/WebP path. Then meshforge_wait.

tools.name: meshforge_wait
tools.description: Wait for a generation job to finish (up to timeout seconds), then meshforge_open_model.

tools.name: meshforge_skeleton
tools.description: The open model's bones: name, parent, role, joint position and rest aim, in character space (+x right, +y up from the floor, +z forward; metres).

tools.name: meshforge_animation_guide
tools.description: How to write an animation spec (aim/rot/root/ease, grounding, anatomy, timing) plus the skeleton. Read before meshforge_build_animation.

tools.name: meshforge_build_animation
tools.description: Keyframe spec → animation on the open rig, played at once. Bones take {aim:[x,y,z], twist} (point the bone that way, character space), {rot:{yaw,pitch,roll}} (degrees from rest), {curl: degrees} (a finger bending toward the palm) or {rest:true}. A key's hands {R, L}: open | relaxed | grip | fist | degrees curls every finger of that hand (rigs with finger bones). root.move [x,y,z] metres (feet are kept on the floor; y = jump height). spec.parts: the parts (meshforge_call listParts) this clip shows, the others hidden in it; leave out to show all. Returns warnings and measurements. replace:true overwrites a clip of the same name.

tools.name: meshforge_contact_sheet
tools.description: Frames of an animation from the front and side (or other views) in one labelled image: the way to judge motion.

tools.name: meshforge_render_frame
tools.description: One picture of the open model, optionally at a time in an animation, from a view (default threeQuarter).

tools.name: meshforge_inspect
tools.description: Numbers for an animation: feet vs floor, foot sliding, loop gap, which bones move, hips travel.

tools.name: meshforge_start_rig
tools.description: Rig the open model in the browser (free): a template skeleton (humanoid, humanoid_tail for lizard/shark folk, quadruped or chain) fitted to the mesh (T- or A-pose). Humanoids get finger and thumb bones where the hands show them (fingers:false to skip). Over ~150k triangles, meshforge_reduce first. facing: which way the model looks in its own space. Then meshforge_render_rig.

tools.name: meshforge_render_rig
tools.description: The model from the front and side with the draft joints drawn on it over a measuring grid (read coordinates off it). Props show purple; pass select to preview a selection in orange.

tools.name: meshforge_set_joints
tools.description: Move draft joints: {jointName: [x, y, z]} in character space. mirror (default true) moves the left/right twin too. Joints belong INSIDE the body.

tools.name: meshforge_free_arm
tools.description: On a rig draft, before binding: cut an arm the model has fused to its body (a sleeve grown into a robe, an arm resting on the side) free along the crease, from the armpit down, and close both sides, so the arm can be raised without dragging the body's skin. side "L" | "R" (the character's own); from: where the cut starts, as a fraction down the upper arm (default 0.35). Leaves the model alone and says why if no clean cut exists. Undo with meshforge_call {method:"restoreArm", args:[{side}]}.

tools.name: meshforge_add_part
tools.description: Put another model from the library on the open one: a tool in a hand (hand_r, hand_l), a pack on the back (back), a hat (head), a pouch at the belt (hip); it rides that joint in every animation. On an unrigged model the only slot is free (stands beside it). It starts at a size that suits the spot (small | auto | large). Adjust or remove with meshforge_call {method:"adjustPart", args:[name, {slot, move:[x,y,z], turn:[x,y,z] degrees, scale}]} / "removePart" / "listParts"; meshforge_save keeps it with the model.

tools.name: meshforge_set_clip_parts
tools.description: Choose which parts an animation shows, so one model carries every tool and load: an axe only in Chop, a pickaxe only in Mine, logs only in Carry. parts: part names from meshforge_call {method:"listParts"} (each lists shownIn); [] hides them all in that clip; null shows them all again. Then meshforge_save.

tools.name: meshforge_split_objects
tools.description: Find the separate objects in the open model, such as a generation of several props (an axe, a pickaxe, a sack) that came back as one mesh. Without save it lists them left to right as seen from the front: index, triangles, center and size. save:true saves each one (or only the indices in objects) as its own library model filed under the original; names gives their names in the same order. gap: touching | close (default) | loose sets how near loose pieces must be to count as one object. Pieces that touch or overlap are one object.

tools.name: meshforge_add_prop
tools.description: Give a prop (axe, sword, shield, staff, lantern) its own rigid bone under parent (usually a hand). Works on a rig draft or on a model already rigged (MeshForge or Meshy). The selection grows along the prop automatically; check with meshforge_render_rig (draft) or meshforge_contact_sheet. On a draft, hold:"hang" first moves a prop that stands apart (a lantern on the ground) into the hand, its top in the fist and the rest hanging below; holdAt:[x,y,z] names the point of the prop to put in the fist instead.

tools.name: meshforge_bind_rig
tools.description: Build the bones and automatic skin weights from the draft: method "heat" (bone heat, as Blender's automatic weights; default) or "nearest" (quicker). Existing animations are retargeted where the skeletons can be matched. Returns a weight check; then meshforge_flex_test.

tools.name: meshforge_fix_weights
tools.description: Find skin that follows the wrong limb (a hand moving part of a foot) and hand it to the bone it sits by. Returns what was fixed and a fresh check.

tools.name: meshforge_flex_test
tools.description: Add a temporary clip (not saved) bending each limb, the spine, head and tail in turn; then meshforge_contact_sheet {animation:"Flex test", samples:12} to spot bad weights.

tools.name: meshforge_preset_animation
tools.description: Free ready-made motion fitted to the open rig: cycles walk | run | idle (bipeds, four-legged rigs, tails) and actions punch | swipe | kick | hit | jump | death | taunt (two-legged rigs). Multipliers speed, stride, arms (for actions: strength), bounce, tail (1 = default). Arms held out at rest (T-pose) hang relaxed; finger rigs get matching hands. parts: the parts this clip shows. Returns measurements.

tools.name: meshforge_reduce
tools.description: Free polygon reduction in the browser to about `triangles` (UVs, textures, rig weights and animations carry over); maxTexture (e.g. 2048) also scales textures down. Then meshforge_save with asNew:true to keep it as a copy.

tools.name: meshforge_remesh
tools.description: Free remesh: rebuild the open model as one clean, even mesh with fresh UVs and its texture baked across (texSize 1024 | 2048 | 4096). quads (e.g. 12000) lays quads that follow the shape (Instant Meshes: edge loops around limbs and fingers; smaller quads where the surface bends tightly, larger on broad areas, or even:true for one size everywhere; better for rigging); otherwise about `triangles` (default 30000) even triangles. Drops any rig: rig it again after. Then meshforge_save with asNew:true; meshforge_export format obj-quads writes the quads.

tools.name: meshforge_save
tools.description: Save the open model (rig and animations) to the MeshForge library. A model saved from MeshForge before is updated; a generated or imported one gets a new entry.

tools.name: meshforge_export
tools.description: Write the open model to disk: glb (default) with every animation, or obj-quads, the surface as an OBJ with quads (exact quads after a quad remesh) for Blender and other editors.

tools.name: meshforge_screenshot
tools.description: Show the MeshForge page. Prefer meshforge_contact_sheet or meshforge_render_rig to judge work.

tools.name: meshforge_open_result
tools.description: Save (if changed) and show MeshForge in visible Chrome with the connector profile, so the user can keep working.
